Floor(Sqrt(-1)) stays complex: Floor is a no-op on a non-real value

caption: Integers are fixed points
A negative integer is unchanged
The imaginary part $-1$ is already an integer
Rounds down: $\lfloor 2.3\rfloor = 2$
Negative integers are fixed
Negatives round away from zero: $\lfloor -2.7\rfloor=-3$
Complex input: each part rounds down, $2-3i$
A division by zero inside Floor leaves Floor(ComplexInfinity), which is not a boxable argument
wolfram.note: Wolfram answers ComplexInfinity; ours leaves Floor(~oo) unevaluated, since a rounding of ~oo is a type error. compute-engine keeps one complex infinity, ~oo, and no directed one (cortex-js/compute-engine#401), so ours follows its model.
sage.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers Floor(ComplexInfinity), and Sage's exact rational division raises a ZeroDivisionError before Floor is even applied.
sympy.note: SymPy answers ComplexInfinity; ours leaves the rounding of ~oo unevaluated, since it is a type error. compute-engine keeps one complex infinity, ~oo, and no directed one (cortex-js/compute-engine#401).
rust.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers "ComplexInfinity", and Rust's exact division panics on the zero denominator before Floor is even applied.
